### [24] [Tokenizer Myths and Where To Find Them](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04215)
*Rylan Schaeffer,Sanmi Koyejo*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Tokenization is a fundamental component of modern language models: before a model sees data, its tokenizer has already determined how the data appears. We identify and challenge three myths in the tokenization research literature. Myth #1: Bits-Per-Byte (BPB) is agnostic to the tokenizer and/or the vocabulary size: BPB is tokens per byte times bits per token, and the two factors do not cancel; using untrained models, we show that BPB prefers some tokenizers over others: the model has learned nothing, but the tokenizer--model pair has. Myth #2: lower BPB means a better model: On untrained models, BPB strongly prefers some vocabulary sizes, even though accuracy remains at chance, and on real models trained on the same data, BPB correlates weakly with downstream performance. Myth #3: different "tokenizer-agnostic" metrics yield consistent results: The "unigram-normalized loss" is not tokenizer-agnostic; its reported correlation of 0.989 with BPB comes from a confounder and falls to 0.057 once fixed; from the same data the two metrics select different vocabularies at each model size. We present a tokenizer trilemma: no metric can score only the true distribution best, give the same predictions the same score, and tie all untrained models, so choosing a metric is choosing a research question. We conclude with a caution for reading the tokenization literature and a conjecture for future work.

### [25] [Sparse Internal Control of Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04349)
*Xizhe Zhang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Language models are increasingly used in text generation, decision support, and automated interaction, creating a need for localized, reversible, and selective control of their behavior. Activation steering demonstrates that internal interventions can alter the behavior of frozen models, but how to select and evaluate compact, multi-site control interfaces remains an open question. I introduce sparse internal control, a framework for steering target behavior by applying inference-time interventions to a small set of internal model nodes. A local target-controllability formulation characterizes candidate site--direction pairs by their behavioral effects and specifies constraints on target recovery, off-target preservation, and intervention energy. Two complementary selectors instantiate this formulation: Driver-OMP selects nodes for sparse reconstruction of a desired behavioral displacement, while Coverage-Driver favors stable coverage across prompts. I propose a six-axis control-evaluation protocol measuring reachability, signed reversal, dose response, feedback controllability, off-target preservation, and held-out reuse. Exploratory experiments on indirect object identification, MMLU multiple-choice question answering, sentiment steering, and refusal steering provide evidence for the feasibility of steering task-defined behavior through sparse internal interventions. The six-axis evaluation characterizes these interventions beyond target movement, revealing distinct control properties that depend on the task and available direction information. Together, the formulation, reference algorithms, and evaluation protocol provide a foundation for the systematic study and development of internal control methods for language models.

### [26] [A Circuit for In-Context Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05344)
*Andrew Gao,William Gao*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: In-context learning (ICL) lets a pretrained language model perform a task specified by demonstrations in its prompt, with no parameter updates. With arbitrary labels the model must acquire a mapping it cannot have memorized, so the learning happens within a single forward pass. Prior work found candidate parts but not how they compose. We give the composition for few-shot sentence classification with arbitrary labels in three 3-4B-parameter transformers. The model implements a key-value memory over label-token positions: each label token's residual stream encodes the label's identity, and middle-layer attention heads write into it the class of the preceding demonstration as its key. At the query, upper-layer heads match the query's class against the stored keys and copy out the matching labels. An early-layer signal encoding whether any label has repeated gates this readout; in its absence the readers attend to the start of the prompt and no label is favored. A separate set of heads suppresses the most recently seen label. Each step is established causally by activation patching, head ablations against random-head baselines, and steering with the model's own signals. A softmax model of the readout with two constants per head, fit on one prompt distribution, predicts another. The computation is conserved across the three models, the named heads alone reproduce the behaviour, and a transformer trained from scratch grows the same parts. The circuit transfers to semantic concepts and to labels with meaning, and the same parts, with a causal gate, appear from 0.6B to 8B in one family and survive instruction tuning. ICL in this setting is a gated associative lookup built from a few identifiable component types, traced causally from demonstrations to prediction.

### [27] [A Conditional Mutual Information Analysis of Response Variety in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03836)
*R. I. Cukier*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models provide a variety of responses at inference (generation) that conventionally depend on a temperature parameter. Using a conditional mutual information approach, a quantitative, entropy based analysis of response variety is given. Three limiting behaviors are defined: arbiter, independent (conditionally) and neutral (deterministic) that span no to maximal mutual information. We give examples of each behavior and suggest their application to: temperature analysis, language analysis, prompt compression, and knowledge graphs.

### [28] [EvoGroup: A Self-Evolving Harness for Group Agents in Shared Contexts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03868)
*Xinyi Xu,Xiaoyang Li,Yucheng Feng,Wenqing Chen,Youliang Yuan,Wei Shi,Rongxiang Weng,Zibin Zheng*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: With the rise of Group Agent such as Claude Tag, agents increasingly serve as digital workers for long-term team collaboration. These agents operate over shared contexts that continuously accumulate through multi-user interactions. However, existing agent memory systems are mainly designed for individual users and struggle to capture group-level knowledge in shared contexts, including group relationships and collaboratively formed knowledge. Manual memory strategies further limit adaptation to diverse and evolving shared contexts. To this end, we propose \textbf{EvoGroup (EvoG)}, a self-evolving harness for group agents that starts from a minimal six-tool cold start and adapts through interaction with shared context. EvoG uses confidence and task outcomes to select informative trajectories, while also eliciting self-reflections on uncertainty in low-confidence cases. The analysis agent then examines selected trajectories through adaptive progressive disclosure, followed by bucketed analysis to synthesize high-level findings that guide the evolve agent in revising the Harness. Empirically, pass@1 on held-out split of EverMemBench improves from 71.07\% to 89.58\%, surpassing both self-evolving memory and human-designed harnesses, including Claude Code (85.83\%). To evaluate generalization, we freeze the evolved harness and evaluate it on the unseen GroupMemBench, where, with GPT-5.5, it demonstrates effective generalization and outperforms both memory baselines and human-designed harnesses.

### [29] [Dory1.0-4B: A Looped Normalized-GPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03998)
*Maxim Fishman,Simeng Sun,Shantanu Acharya,Faisal Ladhak,Brian Chmiel,Santiago Akle Serano,Ron Banner,Boris Ginsburg,Krishna C. Puvvada*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We introduce Dory1.0-4B, a 4-billion-parameter looped (latent-recurrent) language model with elastic depth: a single checkpoint serves different inference compute budgets. Dory1.0-4B is built on a normalized Transformer (nGPT) backbone with interleaved sliding-window and full-attention layers, organized into an input block, a shared recurrent block, and an output block. At inference, the recurrent block can be applied a variable number of times. We pre-trained Dory1.0-4B on 6 trillion tokens. The first 4.5 trillion tokens were trained in NVFP4, and additional pre-training then extended the context length to 256K tokens. Next, we post-trained the model using Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), with a difficulty-aware loop curriculum that routes harder prompts to deeper loops. Increasing the loop count improves accuracy, with the largest gains on coding, agentic, and long-context benchmarks. With two or more loops, Dory1.0-4B outperforms larger models such as Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma 4 12B, and Gemma 4 26B-A4B on average across 12 benchmarks. Looping also makes Dory1.0-4B more token-efficient on agentic benchmarks: with four loops, it generates 1.3-2.5x fewer tokens than with one loop, as the extra computation is spent in latent space rather than on longer outputs. To reduce memory during looping, Dory1.0-4B caches keys and values only from the last loop, keeping its KV-cache footprint equal to that of a non-looped model at any loop count while retaining most of the accuracy gains. We open-source the BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4, and GGUF quantized checkpoints.

### [30] [Same Rule, Different Verdicts: Rubric Language and Clause Structure in LLM Judges for Korean Support Dialogues](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04091)
*Sangdo Han,Moonsoo Kim*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Services that operate in Korean often write their evaluation rubrics in Korean and hand them to an LLM judge. We test whether a judge's verdict depends on the language of the rubric and on how a rubric item is phrased. We write 12 criteria for support dialogues in four clause structures (affirmative, negated, conditional, exception) such that two pairs of structures have the same meaning, and we give each item in Korean and in English. Six low-cost models from three providers, plus one reference model, judge 60 translated ESConv dialogues and 144 constructed boundary cases under every combination (51,744 requests across the seven models). The analysis plan was fixed and committed before data collection. Cross-provider agreement is lower with Korean rubrics than with English rubrics (Cohen's kappa 0.687 vs. 0.745; difference -0.058, 95% CI [-0.072,-0.045]). Disagreement concentrates in negated, conditional, and exception items (odds ratio 5.6 relative to affirmative items). A single model changes its verdict between two items with the same meaning in 11-15% of cases. Two hypotheses are not supported: models from the same provider do not agree more than models from different providers, and adding paired examples does not reduce the language gap. We measure consistency only; no human labels are used, and all materials were drafted by an LLM.

### [31] [Evaluation Contracts and Evaluation Leverage: Sliced-Gap Readings in Structured Prediction Can Move Without Model Change](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04099)
*Hao Lu,Weixing Zhu,Ruiyang Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: NLP evaluation reports routinely cite sliced performance differences, most prominently the intra-inter gap in document-level relation extraction, as capability evidence. We show that such gap readings are joint properties of models and evaluation contracts: scoring function, gold version, threshold, output format, and prompt language. With predictions frozen, a method ordering reverses under a gold-standard exchange (+0.0363, CI excluding zero; tie-level after), movement localizing where gold re-partitions: renames are gauge transformations (Delta=0; re-annotation +0.862). We formalize this as an evaluation leverage account centered on the rank-flip condition. Constructively, the audited evaluation reading (AER) is a contract-marginalized, tie-declared, seed-prescribed, gate-filtered procedure whose tie declarations cover every contract-induced flip on the declared WMT19 grids (14/14; held-out 73% vs. union-of-ties 89%), matching the best single metric contract at epsilon=0.10 equivalence. Evidence spans DocRE, HacRED, a UD probe, and released gold revisions; an alternative-reference-set replication extends it beyond our testbeds. Failed predictions retained as boundaries; a 5% violation gate flags unverifiable settings and bounds survivor-selection bias. We release EvalLever, a preregistered workflow with an amendment trail; on LLM-as-judge grids, the audited ensemble stabilizes every unstable pair (13-15 to zero; generic ensemble shrinkage: the preregistered correlation criterion failed, the companion stabilization criterion passed).

### [32] [Say Less, Mean Better: Training-Free Verbosity Control for Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04107)
*Mahmoud Alyosify,Mirna Imbabi,Eman Elkhamisi,Rahatara Ferdousi*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models (LLMs) often generate responses longer than necessary, increasing inference latency and computational cost. While prompting can encourage conciseness, controlling output length without compromising response completeness remains challenging. Aggressive early stopping can reduce generation costs but risks terminating responses prematurely. We introduce MinimalLM, a training-free framework for reliable verbosity control that combines uncertainty-aware, length-dependent stop-token adjustment with structural completeness guardrails. MinimalLM separates the decision of when to stop from whether stopping is structurally appropriate, coordinating response-level instructions, decoding-time intervention, and completion checks without modifying model parameters or requiring auxiliary models. We evaluate MinimalLM across three open-source LLMs and 330 questions, producing 5,940 responses across baseline and ablation configurations. MinimalLM reduces generated tokens by 47.6%, accelerates individual responses by 19-68%, and eliminates structurally truncated outputs in the primary evaluation. Despite substantial token savings, it achieves an average quality score of 8.04/10, compared with 8.42/10 for unmodified models and 6.46/10 for length-matched truncation. Evaluations across diverse subject domains (such as healthcare, programming, law, and science) demonstrate robust efficiency gains, while ablations establish the complementary roles of decoding control and completeness constraints. Our findings highlight that efficient generation requires more than producing fewer tokens: it requires controlling when generation ends while preserving response integrity. MinimalLM offers a lightweight, training-free approach toward this goal.

### [33] [AdSteer: Native Advertising in Large Language Model Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04147)
*Shuhang Lin,Chuhao Zhou,Zhenyu Wang,Xiao Lin,Changsheng Wang,Saibo Geng,Dimitris N. Metaxas*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language model (LLM) services face rapidly rising serving costs. To sustain free or affordable access for a broad user base, alternative monetization mechanisms are needed. Native advertising offers a promising approach, as it creates economic value by aligning user intent with merchant offerings. Yet how to integrate sponsored content naturally into LLM responses remains largely underexplored. Existing approaches primarily rely on prompt-level injection, multi-pass rewriting, or fine-tuning, which can compromise response quality or introduce additional computational costs. We propose AdSteer, a lightweight decoding-time advertising framework that adaptively adjusts token probabilities to integrate contextually appropriate advertisement into responses. AdSteer calibrates the strength and duration of advertising influence, making sponsored content a natural part of the response. Experiments on GEM-Bench across three application scenarios show that AdSteer achieves an average improvement of 14.1% in overall score over the strongest baselines and 22.5% fewer total tokens on average than rewrite-based methods. These results demonstrate that AdSteer provides an effective and practical solution for native advertising in LLMs.

### [34] [PACT: Certifying What Is Written in Parallel Decoding of Diffusion Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04152)
*Yanchao Li,Yusu Zhang,Jiaqing Xie,Yi Ban,Ben Gao,Zhongyu Huang,Tianfan Fu,Yuqiang Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Parallel decoding speeds up masked diffusion language models by writing several tokens per forward pass. Published commit rules choose these tokens by testing the predicted distributions. Under sampling the written tokens are drawn, and these tests do not see them. We find that answer quality follows the reliability of the tokens actually written. An answer's log probability splits into this reliability and the dependence within each step. We propose PACT, a training-free commit rule that draws the tokens first, certifies the set it will write and spaces the positions of each step apart. This certificate holds at every temperature, and we show that no rule with the same guarantee commits more positions. Experiments use four models of the LLaDA and Dream families and HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, MATH500 and IFEval benchmarks. PACT reaches the quality of published commit rules with fewer forward passes. Spacing removes positions from each step, yet it usually lowers the total cost because later steps then write more tokens. At the same speed, published decoders also write a word twice in a row far more often than PACT. These results suggest that commit rules should certify the tokens they write. Code is available at this https URL .

### [35] [Shared Context Candidate Scoring with Jointly Adapted Readout Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04218)
*Jingyang Du,Yiben Fu,Yang Shen*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Repeated decisions over a shared document create two distinct opportunities: reusing document computation and adapting how question representations score candidate answers. We present Q64, a candidate-scoring system that preserves a frozen 64-layer Qwen3.8-27B text backbone, reuses its hybrid prefix state and intermediate document representations, and jointly trains a residual adapter with a four-layer decoder and candidate-conditioned readout. We used ZiYor, a self-evolving AI system, to explore and refine the Q64 design. We specified the scoring method, implemented the system, and evaluated its accuracy and latency. The final adaptation stage updates 88.66 million parameters using 8,192 selected training views. On a fixed 5,112-item evaluation combining ARC-Challenge, ANLI-R3, and stratified subsets of MMLU-Pro and CMMLU, joint adaptation improves four-benchmark macro accuracy from 66.46% to 74.32%. It remains below the native 27B baseline at 75.68% and AnyJev Qwen3-32B L0 at 76.68%. On a separate synthetic workload with 4,096 document tokens and 50 questions, median cold-request latency is 2.237 seconds, compared with 5.383 seconds for the native baseline and 56.872 seconds for the measured batched AnyJev configuration. Short single-question requests do not share this advantage. The evidence supports an accuracy-latency tradeoff in the evaluated systems, rather than a backbone reduction or an isolated component advantage. Public benchmarks informed earlier development, and real-document multi-question validation remains open.

### [36] [COMPREHEND: Ultra-Fine-Grained Benchmark Understanding by Entailment Hierarchy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04249)
*Sivaraaman Balakrishnan,Prakriti Shetty,Jeremiah Hong,Hamed Zamani,Haw-Shiuan Chang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Understanding what kind of prompts users typically ask and how well an LLM performs on these prompt categories is crucial for LLM practitioners. The existing methods satisfy the demand by hierarchically clustering the user prompts and synthesizing the cluster names using an LLM to build a taxonomy. However, the cluster names from these methods are usually too general for humans to understand the detailed prompt distributions and identify the exact strengths and weaknesses of LLMs. In this study, we propose COMPREHEND, which automatically constructs an ultra-fine-grained entailment hierarchy for the prompts. The entailment hierarchy replaces the cluster names in the taxonomy with sentences to provide more precise cluster descriptions for more fine-grained categorization. Compared with EvalTree, a state-of-the-art taxonomy construction method, COMPREHEND improves an entailment/faithfulness metric from 22.6 to 41.7 and an informative metric from 16.3 to 39.1 in WildBench. Our experiments also show that the weakness report generated based on our entailment hierarchy is much more informative than EvalTree in terms of predicting the response scores in the benchmark. All the code is released in this https URL .

### [37] [Do Multi-Turn Conversational Capabilities Carry Over from Text to Speech? A Parallel Multilingual Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04390)
*Jiaming Zhou,Pei Zhang,Shiwan Zhao,Zhijun Wang,Baosong Yang,Yong Qin*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Successful multi-turn voice interaction requires models to retain information from earlier turns, follow persistent instructions, and track revisions to conversational state. These abilities are usually evaluated from transcripts, leaving open whether successes demonstrated from text carry over when the same turns are spoken, and whether this transfer is consistent across languages. We introduce Omnilingua-AudioMC, a strictly parallel multilingual extension of Audio MultiChallenge, to study this question. The benchmark contains 354 conversations and 1,404 rubric items across ten languages, with content, turn structure, cross-turn dependencies, and evaluation criteria aligned across transcript and speech conditions. Across six speech-language models, the shift from reference transcripts to direct speech input is strongly model- and language-dependent: models with similar transcript performance can diverge substantially under speech, and their relative strengths across languages can change. Paired rubric-level analysis shows that aggregate transcript-speech gaps can obscure which conversational requirements are preserved, because losses of transcript-demonstrated successes can be offset by gains on other items. Replacing preceding user turns, the current turn, or both with model-generated transcripts localizes recoverable degradation: for the two models with the largest gaps, history substitution yields a larger macro-level improvement than current-turn substitution in all ten languages, while the strongest direct-speech model gains little from either. These results show that transcript performance is an unreliable proxy for multilingual spoken conversational ability and identify the representation of preceding spoken context as an important source of recoverable degradation. Our code is publicly available at this https URL .

### [38] [The Min-Max theory of language behavior](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04406)
*Hiram Ring*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: The "Min-Max" theory of language behavior proposes that humans engage simultaneously in minimization of processing effort and maximization of information content, and that this is a primary driver in language evolution (Ring, 2025). This claim seeks to unify observations from language processing (Mahowald et al., 2013; Futrell et al., 2015; Yadav et al., 2020; Hawkins, 2014), interaction (Hörberg and Sjons, 2023; Tucker et al., 2025; Jaeger and Tily, 2011; Smith and Culbertson, 2025), and corpora (Levshina and Moran, 2021; Levshina, 2023; Newmeyer, 2017), which suggest that considerations of processing efficiency and information content are both implicated in human communication. The interaction between these two processes provides an explanation for human linguistic behavior at various levels (Linders and Louwerse, 2023) and predicts historical developments in language, i.e. related to word order (Ring, 2025). Given that the original formulation of the Min-Max theory is based on observational data, the current paper seeks to validate the theory mathematically. Through a series of experiments that use computational models to investigate the theory's predictions, pretrained and iterated learning models are queried with synthetic data. The experiments show that manipulating the variables of token length and the weight of information content in a tabula rasa model results in word order change, as predicted by the theory. The experiments also identify important differences between computational models and observations of human language data, suggesting that current transformer-based language models may not accurately represent psycholinguistic processes. The overall findings indicate that evolutionary trajectories in language are highly susceptible to minimization of processing and maximization of information content.

The experiments also identify important differences between computational models and observations of human language data, suggesting that current transformer-based language models may not accurately represent psycholinguistic processes. The overall findings indicate that evolutionary trajectories in language are highly susceptible to minimization of processing and maximization of information content.

</details>


### [39] [Typological Feature Induction as a Benchmark for Inductive Metalinguistic Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04421)
*Chen Zhang,Seth Aycock,Yusuke Miyao*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Existing metalinguistic reasoning benchmarks require both inference of rules and their application, making failures hard to diagnose. We introduce typological feature induction (TFI) which targets the former step. Given sentences in an unnamed language paired with translations in a known pivot language, models must predict a typological feature of the unnamed language. From Grambank and multi-parallel corpora, we automatically build evaluation questions over 195 languages. We find that LLMs identify 59--80% of these languages from only 16 sentence pairs; and misaligning the translations barely affects their accuracy, suggesting reliance on prior knowledge of the language. Enciphering text to prevent recognition increases the corpus' utility, but mainly for features where target and pivot languages agree. On languages which models cannot identify, neither open model outperforms a majority-value baseline. Since induction from raw text aligns with field linguists' use-case, this work indicates the models tested are not yet ready for this role. TFI offers a scalable path to track progress in this direction.

### [40] [ReListen: Training-Free Evidence Localization in Hour-Long Audio with Frozen Audio Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04480)
*Ming-Hao Hsu,Shujie Liu,Yuxuan Hu,Yuxiang Wang,Yingda Shen,Jinyu Li,Zhizheng Wu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Audio language models are meant to answer questions from the audio itself, but an hour-long recording rarely fits in their context, and the answer often depends on a few seconds of it. Transcribing the recording first makes it fit but discards sounds and voices, while systems that return to the audio must be trained for this behavior. We propose ReListen, a training-free method in which a frozen audio language model finds its own evidence before answering. In a Jev-style scan, the model scores each 20-second window by the probability that it helps answer the question, and it then answers from the highest-scoring minute. This minute overlaps the annotated evidence far more often than transcript retrieval, for 88.5% of VoiceGiraffe questions. Without any change, the same scan also grounds events on LAT-Bench as well as a model trained for temporal grounding. Answering from it matches or exceeds hearing the whole recording with a small fraction of the audio, and on VoiceGiraffe it exceeds a transcript of the whole recording by 9.2 points. The selected evidence is also worth hearing rather than reading. Given the same excerpts, reading their transcript matches listening on speech content, but listening is clearly more accurate on questions about sounds and voices. Moreover, ReListen answers faster than every transcript-based system, and its memory stays constant even for recordings too long to hear whole on one GPU. Therefore, a frozen audio language model can search hour-long recordings by itself, without a transcript or additional training.

### [41] [TEMPO: Time Series Understanding via Discrete Tokenization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04482)
*Riccardo Maggioni*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Time-series interpretation often requires both numerical observations and textual context. Integrating these inputs into a pretrained language model raises a representation question: how should a signal enter the model's token sequence? We present TEMPO, which extends an LLM's vocabulary with discrete codes from a context-aware Transformer tokenizer using finite scalar quantization. A frozen tokenizer maps four-step patches to a 625-code vocabulary; signal tokens, scale statistics, and text are then processed by the LLM's existing self-attention layers. Adaptation updates the new token embeddings and DoRA adapters. With a Qwen3-4B backbone and task-specific fine-tuning, TEMPO achieves macro-F1 scores of 89.0% on activity recognition, 85.0% on sleep staging, and 86.0% on bearing-fault diagnosis. Time-series question answering and qualitative bearing-diagnosis examples further illustrate how this interface combines signal representations with textual context. Together, these results demonstrate the utility of discrete vocabulary extension for time-series understanding.

### [42] [Evaluating LLMs as Judges of Counterspeech Quality Against Online Hate Speech](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04627)
*Johnny Alali,Nicolás Benjamín Ocampo,Davide Ceolin*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Prolonged exposure to hate speech on social media can cause lasting psychological distress among users. Counterspeech has emerged as an effective, non-censorial mitigation strategy, but its deployment requires rigorous quality assessment. Manual assessment is unscalable due to the large volume of content on the Web and imposes severe emotional strain on human annotators. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a scalable alternative, yet concerns remain regarding their reliability. In this paper, we investigate the extent to which LLMs can effectively perform this task. We test 12 open-weight LLMs of different sizes and families under zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting, to approximate pointwise and pairwise human expert assessment of counterspeech quality across four dimensions: relevance, coherence, aggressiveness, and suitableness. We find that (i) LLMs show low agreement and moderate rank correlations with human experts: our best configuration, Qwen 2.5 72B on coherence, achieves up to a linear-weighted Cohen's $\kappa_l = 0.19$ and Spearman's $\rho = 0.42$ in pointwise evaluation and an unweighted Cohen's $\kappa = 0.25$ in pairwise evaluation. (ii) Converting pointwise scores into pairwise labels substantially improves human--LLM agreement for selected configurations. For same-instance coherence, Qwen 2.5 72B under zero-shot prompting achieves $\kappa = 0.35$ with converted labels, compared with $\kappa = 0.25$ when judging pairs directly, and Mixtral 8$\times$7B under few-shot prompting improves from $\kappa = 0.07$ to $\kappa = 0.34$. (iii) LLMs agree more with one another than with human experts, particularly in pairwise evaluation, where the strongest model pair, OLMo 2 32B and Llama 3.3 70B on coherence, reaches substantial agreement with $\kappa = 0.76$, whereas their agreement with the experts in the same configuration does not exceed $\kappa = 0.21$.

### [43] [MIMIC-Note-Extract: A Large-Scale Structured Dataset Extracted from MIMIC-IV-Note Discharge Summaries](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04685)
*Kristian Schwethelm,Jonas Kuntzer,Conrad Ketzer,Eva Wende,Moritz Schlager,Daniel Rueckert,Georgios Kaissis,Friederike Jungmann,Paul Hager*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: MIMIC is one of the most widely used public hospital datasets for machine learning on electronic health records, yet clinically important information, such as past medical history, allergies, and diagnostic findings, remains confined to free-text discharge summaries. Studies requiring this information must therefore build their own extraction pipelines, duplicating substantial effort across projects. We release MIMIC-Note-Extract (MNE), a large-scale dataset that uses a hybrid extraction pipeline combining deterministic parsing with schema-guided large language model generation to transform 16 sections from 300,720 discharge summaries into structured tables. MNE adds information that has no structured MIMIC counterpart and enriches related tables with broader coverage and greater clinical detail, including 10 times more patient-history entries and medication histories for more than twice as many admissions. Validation by medical doctors confirms extraction accuracy above 92% across sections. Using MNE, we construct a clinical decision-making benchmark for LLM agents, demonstrating how reusable structured representations of clinical narratives reduce data curation effort.

### [44] [CardioVascBench:Prioritized Diagnosis Generation from Real-World Chinese Cardiovascular Records](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04687)
*Minghao Kong,Muyao Chen,Jianhao Wu,Yuqiang Zhang,Xiangbin Meng,Zirong Liu,Ting Cao,Kaida Ning,Zhen Song,Rongjie Wang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Identifying the primary diagnosis alone does not fully characterize a model's diagnosis-generation performance. We introduce CardioVascBench, a retrospective benchmark for prioritized diagnosis generation from real-world Chinese cardiovascular inpatient records. It contains 3,262 de-identified cases, with 2,174 for training and 1,088 for evaluation, linking clinical narratives and textual ECG reports to expert-verified, ordered discharge diagnoses standardized to ICD-10. An English translation of the evaluation set supports aligned cross-lingual comparison. Our evaluation protocol combines terminology normalization and rank-aware scoring to separately assess primary-diagnosis identification, reference-diagnosis coverage, and list precision. Evaluation across 36 systems shows that higher primary-diagnosis accuracy does not necessarily imply higher list precision against discharge references. We also provide CardioKG-Agent, a knowledge-enhanced baseline combining entity normalization, constrained graph retrieval, and guideline evidence. In a staged comparison of three baseline models, supervised fine-tuning plus the agent achieves a 73.5% higher mean composite score than fine-tuning alone, representing a system-level gain. These results measure retrospective agreement with recorded diagnoses; agreement between metric rankings and physician judgments remains to be validated. CardioVascBench supports research on diagnosis prioritization and knowledge-enhanced generation.

### [45] [TraceRouter++: Causal Semantic Routing Realignment via Optimal Transport](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04878)
*Chuancheng Shi,Shangze Li,Wenhua Wu,Hengzhi Chen,Fei Shen,Li Zhuo,Zhiyong Wang,Tat-Seng Chua*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Despite their remarkable capabilities, large foundation models (LFMs) remain susceptible to adversarial manipulation. Current safety intervention methods primarily rely on the \textit{locality hypothesis}, rigidly suppressing isolated neurons or features. However, harmful semantics manifest as distributed, cross-layer circuits, rendering localized ablations both brittle against complex jailbreaks and detrimental to general utility. To bridge this gap, we propose TraceRouter++, a routing-level safety intervention framework that explicitly traces safety-relevant causal routing pathways activated under harmful inputs and realigns their unsafe activation states. Our framework operates in a \textit{Discover-Trace-Realign} paradigm: it first pinpoints a sensitive onset layer via attention divergence and disentangles dense activations into interpretable routing features using sparse autoencoders (SAEs). Subsequently, it maps these features to downstream causal circuits via feature influence scores (FIS). Crucially, departing from rigid suppression paradigms, TraceRouter++ introduces a constrained optimal transport (OT)-based soft routing realignment. By formulating safety intervention as a tractable coordinate-wise marginal optimal transport approximation, our method redirects unsafe activation marginals toward safe-reference marginals within causally identified routing subspaces while preserving non-selected coordinates at the intervention point. This mechanism safely redirects malicious semantic flows while leaving orthogonal computational routes intact. Extensive experiments across representative large language models (LLMs), multimodal large language models (MLLMs), and diffusion models (DMs) show that TraceRouter++ outperforms evaluated baselines, improving adversarial robustness while maintaining a favorable safety-utility trade-off. WARNING: This paper contains unsafe model responses.

### [46] [PROSE: Preservation-Constrained Selective Editing for Guilty Bias in Legal Judgment Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04921)
*Yimeng Wang,Zeyuan Tian,Xinyu Wang,Danyang Gao,Chenglei Shen,Zhongxiang Sun,Lei La,Weijie Yu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Legal judgment prediction models may retain a guilty verdict after a legally decisive condition has been altered such that the specified charge is no longer established. We study this guilty bias via selective repair over matched charge-established and charge-not-established cases, where the unsupported verdict should change while its supported counterpart remains stable. We construct CAIL-MC, a legally reviewed dataset of 11,478 matched pairs covering 261 Chinese criminal charges. Held-out activation interventions show that contrasts learned from correctly resolved pairs transfer to false-guilty cases, but target-reaching interventions can also damage matched supported-guilty decisions. Motivated by this observation, we introduce PROSE, which reconstructs case-specific targets from a training-derived residual geometry, aligns them with a local margin-descent signal, attenuates supported-guilty-sensitive components, and realizes bounded targets through a preservation-regularized low-rank parameter update. Across Qwen3-8B and GLM4-9B, PROSE achieves stronger pairwise safe repair and evidence sensitivity, while preserving standard single-pass inference.

### [47] [Residual Attribute Leakage Is an Interface: Auditing Privacy Evaluation After Text De-identification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04941)
*Tuan Thanh Duong,Joongmin Shin,Jeongho Yoon,Junyoung Son,Heuiseok Lim*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: A privacy evaluation of de-identified text asks a language model (the adversary) to guess a person's protected attribute. We introduce a prior-normalised clipped leakage score of its confidence gain on the true value and audit the conclusions drawn from it. Each verdict depends on an evaluation interface (the queried person, answer options, prior, adversary model and scoring rule), which we vary on fixed releases of three corpora. In a stress test, an editor that writes the opposite-sex form at the same spans a redaction editor would redact misleads the adversary about most people, yet ranks first among editors scored on the same MedQA entries under this score, as under attack accuracy and proper scoring rules read as privacy. A relabelling-invariant reading of AUC ranks that editor sixth of eight, and a rule-aware adversary recovers the attribute from the same text. On ordinary releases most verdict changes are gains or losses of separability; of six choices varied over all pairs, only the adversary reverses comparisons (5 of its 124 changes), and the query can target the wrong person. SACC, a traceable editor we build as the instrument, lets us ablate two editing principles and show where its advantage does not hold.

### [48] [HERIT: Enabling Global Access to Hanja-to-English Historical Translation by Mitigating Temporal Bias](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04949)
*Dayeon Jeong,Kyeongpil Kang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Historical archives are invaluable for multidisciplinary research but remain inaccessible globally due to severe language barriers. While manual translation is prohibitively expensive and time-consuming, simply applying existing machine translation models is inadequate due to unique linguistic nuances and the temporal bias inherent in scarce human-labeled corpora. To address these challenges, we propose HERIT, a systematic domain-adaptation pipeline that leverages retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to generate high-quality pseudo-labeled data from abundant Hanja-Korean corpora. This approach substantially expands the training dataset, mitigating both data scarcity and temporal overfitting across different historical periods. Extensive automated and human evaluations demonstrate that HERIT consistently outperforms baselines. Finally, we translate previously untranslated portions of the archives using our model, thereby enabling global access to these resources for researchers.

### [49] [Whose Effect Is It? How Objectives Inflate Learned Subspace Interventions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05033)
*Toygar Tanyel,Serkan Ayvaz*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Interpretability often locates concepts by copying part of a language model's state from one input into another (activation patching). A larger output change counts as stronger evidence that this part carries the concept. Methods that learn which part to copy often change the output more than the whole state does. By that reading, learned parts isolate the concept more cleanly. Yet the whole contains the part. So whose effect is this excess, the network's or the method's? Copying the whole state learns nothing, so it shows what the network produces. We prove that, to first order, the effects of orthogonal parts add up to that of the whole. A part therefore exceeds the whole exactly when the rest moves the output back, which does not require isolating the concept more cleanly. Objectives that reward a larger effect select such parts. Distributed alignment search with cross-entropy, for example, exceeds the whole-state copy just before the output on almost all tasks, and inside the network at most sites. In both, changing only its objective to target what the network produces removes most of the excess. It therefore comes largely from the objective, so a larger learned effect alone is not stronger evidence.

### [50] [ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05036)
*Guanting Dong,Zhichao Sun,Xinyu Yang,Rui Wang,Xin Deng,Jiajie Jin,Zhixiong Yang,Junhao Huang,Han Han,Mingyu Ma,Xiaotao Wang,Yuyang Hu,Xiaoshuai Song,Xiaoxi Li,Jiejun Tan,Zhecan Wang,Shihan Dou,Honglin Guo,Zhiheng Xi,Tao Gui,Tao Ji,Qi Zhang,Yutao Zhu,Ji-Rong Wen,Zhicheng Dou*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models are deployed as long-horizon agents that compose diverse tools across MCP services into executable workflows. Existing MCP environment-scaling methods are data-centric: they first synthesize a database and scenario, then derive tools and tasks from them. As a result, tool interfaces may not match real ones, tool compositions are not grounded in execution, and tasks rarely span more than one environment. We propose ToolSpace, a tool-centric framework that reverses this order. ToolSpace mines data, state, and retry dependencies from adjacent calls in execution traces of real MCP services and open agent corpora, using deterministic rules rather than LLM judgment, and clusters the resulting weighted tool-composition graph into environments. Databases are synthesized only for state-mutating environments, while query and stateless tools replay recorded returns. ToolSpace then performs state-aware random walks with rollback and decompiles each chain into a natural-language task with assertion-based checks, keeping only samples that replay successfully from the initial state. Applied to AutomationBench and tau3-Bench Banking, the pipeline produces harder Pro versions on which 7 frontier models drop by up to 38.2 points. Across seven long-horizon tool-use benchmarks, ToolSpace raises Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 23.0 to 41.0 average score (43.2 with RL) and GLM-5.2 from 44.6 to 56.6, on par with Claude Opus 5. Ablations show that execution-witnessed edges clearly outperform LLM-judged ones, and performance keeps improving with data and environment scale.

### [51] [GM League Arena: An Interactive Long-Horizon Task Benchmark Based on Professional Sports League Management](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05147)
*Junkai Zhou,Ziming Pan,Zhaoyi Zhang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Long-horizon decision-making under sustained competition requires large language models (LLMs) to balance immediate investment with future resource needs. However, local success in multi-step interactions can not adequately capture cumulative decision effects or demonstrate long-term goal achievement under resource constraints and sustained competition. To address this gap, we introduce GM Bench, a benchmark for managing professional sports teams across seasons under resource constraints and competition among teams. We build the environment simulators for four sports and add financial constraints, player demands, and market mechanisms to establish a unified task across sports. Diverse rosters of comparable strength are constructed from real-world player data, and each LLM is evaluated as a team general manager to assess its long-term management capabilities. We evaluate competitive performance, cash reserves, and cross-season improvement across four sports. Over five NBA seasons, Claude Opus 5.5 ranks first among 29 LLMs, while GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol combine strong performance with larger cash reserves.

### [52] [When Self-Verification Hurts: Calibrated Answer Repair for Financial Question Answering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05166)
*Celine Guo,Weida Liang,Yujian Fu,Anqi Dang,Yanzheng Jin,Kenji Kawaguchi,Wenya Wang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Financial question answering can fail even when a model extracts a plausible number from the supplied evidence: the answer may attach it to the wrong entity, period, unit, or accounting concept. Asking the model to verify and revise its draft can help, but open-ended revision may alter content that was already correct or inspect the wrong relation and reinforce the original error. We formulate repair as a decision that balances the information it may recover against the correct content it may damage. Based on this trade-off, we introduce Calibrated Answer Repair (CAR), which first estimates whether a draft is likely to benefit from repair, then selects a targeted check, localizes the relevant evidence or draft span, and limits the permitted edit. Across FinRank, Fin-RATE, and FinQA with three open-weight models, CAR outperforms generic verification in all dataset-model settings. At the system level, it recovers 14.6% of initially missed answer requirements while damaging 2.1% of initially correct ones. Its post-draft token cost is over 30 percent lower than the iterative revision alternatives. Ablations on two dataset-model settings show that evidence localization and bounded editing are the main contributors to CAR's gains.

### [53] [ARLoop: Fully-Open Pre-trained Looped Transformers with Attention Residuals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05234)
*Yuekun Yao,Yupei Du,Dawei Zhu,Huan Sun*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Looped transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying a shared set of transformer layers, offering a parameter-efficient way to scale computation. However, standard residual connections aggregate information across recurrent depth into a single stream, providing limited control over which intermediate representations from preceding layers should be reused. In this paper, we introduce ARLoop, a looped transformer architecture based on attention residuals, where the input of each layer is selectively aggregated through attention over model depth. Distinct from standard transformers, we find that looped transformers do not require access to the full residual history: sliding-window depth attention matches or outperforms full-history attention at larger recurrent depths. Across controlled experiments with multiple parameter scales (140M and 370M) and recurrent depths (R = 1 to 5), ARLoop consistently outperforms prior residual designs for looped transformers. More importantly, we further scale ARLoop to 0.6B and 1.2B parameters under a realistic LLM pretraining recipe, demonstrating that the gains transfer to realistic pretraining, with particularly strong improvements on math and coding tasks. Our 1.2B model, pretrained on only 0.5T tokens with three recurrences, outperforms Huginn-3.5B (the only fully-open looped LLM as of our release date) across all evaluated tasks and is competitive with similar-sized non-looped models such as Qwen3.5-2B despite being trained on substantially less data.

### [54] [MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05313)
*Dian Jin,Jinluan Yang,Kairong Han,Baohong Li,Zijing Hu,Yi He,Wenlin Zhong,Yunze Tong,Minqin Zhu,Linchuan Li,Yanan Niu,Kun Kuang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Skill memories encode past experiences as textual prompts to improve reinforcement learning (RL) for self-evolving agents. Complementing RL, On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) provides dense, fine-grained supervision to internalize knowledge from skill-guided trajectories and accelerate policy learning. However, self-generated memories often contain noisy supervision and functionally entangled, redundant, or conflicting knowledge, making direct distillation difficult. Under limited training budgets, these issues can hinder knowledge internalization and even degrade performance. To address this problem, we propose MDSKILL, a multi-view distillation approach for skill memory internalization. MDSKILL organizes skill memories into three complementary functional views (state grounding, action planning, and execution control) and selects high-quality skills using dynamic metrics to construct view-specific and integrated reasoning branches. OPSD then transfers and consolidates complementary experiential knowledge across these branches into a shared policy, enabling efficient skill internalization and continuous agent self-evolution. We evaluate MDSKILL on three agent benchmarks against RL, skill-augmented, and self-distillation baselines that do not rely on stronger external teacher models. Without additional computational overhead, MDSKILL improves upon SOTA performance by up to 7.1% and 8.1% on ALFWorld and WebShop. Extensive ablations and evolution analyses further validate its effectiveness in knowledge internalization and policy improvement. The code is available at this https URL .

### [55] [Can Network Models of Science Do Without Pluralist Agents?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04590)
*Jonas Hallgren,David Hyland,Mahault Albarracin*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: 本文提出并检验了一种基于主动推断/多智能体变分推断的“认识论多元主义”网络模型，比较能同时持有并权衡多个竞争理论（多元智能体）与只能维护单一信念分布的单一理论智能体（单元智能体）社区。结果表明：社区能否改变所信奉的理论取决于“模型支持度”（理论偏好/裁决）的传播，而非理论内部预测值的传播——共享预测只改善精度，共享对某一理论的支持才促成范式转换；多元智能体还能表现出可测量的“危机期”不确定性上升。结论是：科学网络模型不能省去多元智能体，若要帮助而非窄化科学，AI系统应能同时持有多个理论，并区分“理论内信念”与“理论间支持”。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 费耶阿本德（Feyerabend）主张科学的有效性依赖于人们敢于持有并辩护与既定理论不相容的竞争理论（理论多元主义），因为一个理论的失败往往只有在与之不相容的替代理论面前才会显现；单一理论范式（库恩的常规科学）则会掩盖自身反常。历史上两种观点的优劣多靠案例论证，难以直接检验，因而需要可计算模型。同时，随着LLM被引入科研流程，需要回答AI系统应具备何种世界表征才能避免“局部正确但理论前提根本错误”的路径。现有网络认识论、意见动力学与主动推断模型多只处理单一信念层面，未区分“在某理论下的条件信念”与“对理论本身的支持度”这两个层级。

Method: 构建N个智能体在固定网络上的同步多轮模型。每个智能体持有K个候选理论（各为贝叶斯网/线性高斯结构，共享可观测坐标、各有特有潜变量），状态由两部分构成：理论内的信念密度ρ_{ik,t}(x_k)（以对数支持a_{ik,t}参数化的模型概率q_{ik,t}表达理论偏好）。通信分两个独立通道：理论内信念共享用加权对数意见池（归一化几何池），模型支持共享用对数线性社会学习规则（混合系数α_m）。观测更新被形式化为最小化变分自由能（复杂度KL + 准确性），随后施加参考锚定（保留参数ω，形式上亦为加权KL目标）以表示背景理论承诺的持续性。实验以18世纪燃素说与氧气说的竞争为动机案例：两理论共享可观测量（燃烧程度C、气体净吸收G、固体质量变化M），各有潜变量P（燃素释放）与O（氧气并入），结构系数±0.8；环境为三高斯噪声观测，用注意力权重实现选择性观测。三个对照实验：(1) 完全观测下信号从(1,1,-1)翻转为(1,1,1)后的延迟修正；(2) 选择性观测下8名气体观测者与8名质量观测者，比较私有/共享模型支持与单一高斯对照；(3) 证据改变后仅改变通信通道的四种条件。补充实验比较环、轮辐、社区、完全图拓扑。度量指标包括理论选择（氧理论支持度q_O）、个体模型熵、群体数值分歧距离、MSE与NLL，各50次运行、2000次自助重采样置信带。

Result: 1) 完全观测：社区先偏好燃素说，质量信号翻转后经一段延迟才转向氧气说；期间个体模型熵上升（对应科学“危机”），随后随信心恢复而下降，说明模型能区分“解释改变”与“数值调整”。2) 选择性观测：模型支持私有时，气体观测者偏好燃素说、质量观测者偏好氧气说；共享模型支持后两群体均转向氧气说。但质量观测者的氧气支持几乎不受是否共享影响，而气体观测者的偏好却关键依赖质量观测者所共享的支持信息——即只传预测不足以改变偏好。单一高斯对照也呈现群体数值分歧，说明数值差距不等同于理论对立，且差距越大不意味预测越好。3) 通道消融（证据改变后）：仅共享模型支持（单独或配合理论内共享）时受限群体的氧支持在窗口内趋近1，私有支持则达不到；理论内共享在此之上进一步加速修正并降低晚期MSE。效应不统一：仅共享理论内信念对受限群体预测只有有限改善且使氧理论信念上升更慢，而完全观测者开启该通道反而晚期MSE略高。4) 拓扑：完全图与以枢纽为核心的轮辐图上修正传播最快，社区图最慢，环图在时程末仍在上升。5) 分析性结论（附录0.A.4）：两候选的对数支持差满足z_{i,t+1}=(1-α_m)z_{i,t}+α_m Σ_j W^m z_{j,t}+s_{i,t}，即“裁决”是可传播的独立状态；理论内共享虽在α_m=0时也能间接影响s从而影响偏好，但速度更慢。

Conclusion: 回答标题问题：不能省略多元智能体。单元智能体只能分享估计值，多元智能体还能分享“支持哪个理论”，两类消息产生不同的信念动力学；只知道理论预测什么，并不能让人知道是否应当采纳它，单元模型在结构上无法体现这一差别。多元智能体还能“察觉自己的解释发生了变化”，这接近费耶阿本德关于失败只有在替代理论对照下才显现的洞见。对AI（含LLM）的启示：把所有观测折叠进单一解释的LLM类似单元智能体，只能精炼理论而无法察觉竞争理论更能解释数据；只总结各理论预测而不追踪证据支持哪一理论的LLM则只会分享估计、从不给出裁决。作者强调结论的限度：候选理论、观测安排与注意力权重预先给定，智能体不发明替代理论、不修改图结构、不自主选择实验、不筛选报告，因此结果未证明“显式潜变量图”或“多元主义促进科学发现”，只是展示了保留多个候选使“理论支持”与“数值调整”可分离；此外尚未检验理论内部结构的重要性、被削弱的理论是否值得保留、以及允许智能体自主选择实验后网络结构对发现与长期预测的影响，这些是后续方向。

Abstract: Science is a process of useful models being proven wrong time and again, but despite its many flaws, it somehow works. Why is this? Paul Feyerabend argued that it works because people dare to hold and defend incompatible rival theories against the accepted one, since a theory's failures often lead to its abandonment in the presence of a more accurate or simpler alternative. He called this view theoretical pluralism. We introduce a theoretical and experimental model in which this can be examined. It compares communities of pluralist agents, which can hold rival theories side by side and maintain beliefs within and between those theories, with communities of monist agents, which can only incorporate what they hear or observe into a single model of their own. In a multi-agent variational inference setting, our experimental demonstrations illustrate how communities with rival theories can go through periods of uncertainty followed by a shift in the theories they hold true, how the information that is communicated between communities affects beliefs when those communities make different observations about the world, and how sharing support for theories and sharing beliefs within them contribute differently to collective belief dynamics.

</details>


### [56] [GeoFaham: Domain-Specialized Multi-Agent Geospatial Analytics for Disaster Response](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04977)
*Muhammad Sohail Danish,Gilles Q. Hacheme,Akram Zaytar,Satej S. Soman,Inbal Becker-Reshef,Juan Lavista Ferres,Salman Khan,Girmaw Abebe Tadesse*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: GeoFaham 是一个面向灾害响应地理空间分析的领域专用多智能体系统：由 Orchestrator 通过双账本（任务账本 + 进度账本）控制循环协调 Vector、Maps、STAC、Raster 四个专用智能体，并通过 Response Store 在 LLM 上下文之外持久化带类型元数据的地理空间产物，智能体之间只交换紧凑 ID 与摘要。配套提出 GeoFaham-Bench（40 个任务、17 条真实灾害记录、非刚性评测）。在 GeoFaham-Bench 上，GeoFaham 总分 0.940，优于 Codex（0.879）、Claude Code（0.837）、OpenCode（0.780），且 token 用量减少约 7.5 倍。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 灾害响应的地理空间决策支持往往需要跨源、跨阶段的长链工作流（灾害数据库、OSM 地图要素、卫星影像、栅格产品、可复用产物），正确性取决于空间范围、时间窗口与中间执行状态的保持。通用 LLM 与编码智能体在地理空间上有特有失效模式：无法承载大体量产物、选错证据源、丢失 CRS/时间/波段等元数据、执行无效几何操作（如在经纬度上做度量计算、忽略无效几何）。现有工作要么只覆盖单一遥感源（ThinkGeo、UnivEARTH 等），要么只考察单智能体是否从固定函数集中正确调用工具（GeoBenchX、GeoAnalystBench 等），缺少跨源协作、中间产物管理与失败恢复能力的评测。此外，精确匹配评测不适用于允许多条有效执行轨迹的地理空间任务，需要非刚性评测协议。

Method: 架构：三项原则——有界专业化（每个智能体窄动作空间、领域提示与统一输出契约）、状态接地的编排（中间产物进入任务状态，支撑计划/派发/恢复/综合）、产物感知记忆（大体量产物留在 LLM 上下文之外）。Orchestrator 采用双账本嵌套控制循环：外层任务账本做事实抽取（意图、灾害上下文、时间约束、AOI、目标实体、所需空间操作）与依赖感知计划；内层进度账本跟踪完成/待办步骤、响应 ID、产物元数据与失败，派发前执行计划一致性、输入有效性、地理空间兼容性三项检查（几何类型、CRS、边界、时间覆盖、模式），失败时回到外层重规划（调整空间范围、扩展时间窗、切换影像集合、拆解任务、改派专家）。Response Store 为会话级文件持久化产物注册表，记录唯一 ID、来源、摘要、路径与类型化元数据（矢量：几何类型/CRS/边界/要素数/属性模式；影像栅格：时间覆盖/波段/分辨率/边界/CRS/统计量），智能体通过符号占位符（如空间 SQL 中的 artifact ID）在执行层解析为真实几何以保证确定性计算。四个智能体：Vector Agent（PostGIS 空间查询、join、缓冲、距离过滤、聚合、产物生成）、Maps Agent（OSM 道路/设施/边界/水系检索，每次调用一类要素）、STAC Agent（按空间/时间/集合/云量/波段检索影像并校验覆盖）、Raster Agent（沙箱 Python + xarray/rasterio/geopandas 生成光谱指数、变化检测、淹没与火烧分析、栅格转矢量、分区统计）。基准：GeoFaham-Bench 含 40 个面向用户的灾害响应问题、17 条 2023–2025 真实灾害记录（火灾、洪水、飓风、气旋、地震、龙卷风），10 类任务，24/40 为 hard；由地理空间专家定义上下文与期望、LLM 提出工作流、专家逐步校验的非刚性 ground truth（空间/时间/方法/输出层不变量与容差）。评测采用 LLM-as-judge（GPT-5.2）：跨系统协议 13 维/5 类（任务结果 0.35、地理空间方法 0.30、可复现性 0.15、合规 0.10、鲁棒性 0.10）；内部过程协议 11 维/4 类（规划 0.27、执行 0.38、合规 0.17、输出 0.18）；并记录诊断旗标。实验对比 Codex(GPT-5.1)、Claude Code(Claude Sonnet 4.6)、OpenCode(GPT-5.1)，共享任务、数据源、库与执行环境；内部消融 C1–C4 分配 GPT-4o/GPT-5.1 至不同角色。

Result: 跨系统：GeoFaham 总分 0.940（S_out 0.897、S_meth 0.951、S_repr 0.982、S_comp 0.999、S_rob 0.933），较 Codex 0.879、Claude Code 0.837、OpenCode 0.780 分别领先 6.1/10.3/16.0 分。最大增益集中在数据选择正确性（0.972，超最强基线 11.9/16.0/15.3 分）与时空逻辑（0.918，超 13.9 分）；而实现正确性（0.922）与几何数据完整性（0.997）各系统接近或基线更优（Claude Code 0.934），说明优势来自证据选择与依赖协调而非代码生成。产物质量 0.976 最高。消融：C1（全 GPT-4o）0.808 → C2（仅升级规划器）0.914（+10.6 分）→ C3（再升级进度跟踪、Vector、Raster）0.964 最佳 → C4（全部 GPT-5.1）0.959 略低，表明强模型应集中在规划、监控、空间查询生成与栅格编程，受限检索角色可用弱模型；错误率由 61.3% 降至 33.8%/28.8%，C2/C3/C4 均恢复全部错误，C3/C4 重规划频次显著更低（3.8%/5.0%）。效率：GeoFaham 平均 106,344 tokens/任务、169.64 秒，Codex 795,352 tokens（7.5×）、Claude Code 285,100（2.7×）、OpenCode 376,042（3.5×）；OpenCode 最快（128.37 秒）但得分最低；C3 的 token 低于 C1/C2，说明选择性分配强模型同时提升效果与效率。

Conclusion: 可靠的地理空间智能体不仅需要可执行代码，更需要显式的时空接地、产物依赖验证与中间结果的持久化管理。GeoFaham 的价值主要体现在正确的证据与灾害/AOI 选择、时空范围保持、跨源依赖协调与可追溯的产物传递上，而非单纯提升编码质量；架构原则（专业分工 + 校验编排 + 产物感知记忆）并不限于灾害场景，可推广至其他多源地理空间分析。局限：基准仅 40 个任务、覆盖有限的传感器与人道数据集与灾害情形，且依赖 OSM、卫星目录等动态外部源，ground truth 需采用容差与语义检查；实现基于对话式智能体框架的闭源多智能体团队，评测依赖 LLM-as-judge 主观评分。

Abstract: Real-world geospatial decision support requires more than single-step retrieval or code generation. Disaster-response questions often involve multi-source workflows that combine spatial databases, map-derived features, satellite imagery, raster products, and reusable geospatial artifacts, where correctness depends on preserving spatial scope, temporal context, and intermediate execution state. While large language models and coding agents offer a promising interface for such workflows, they struggle with geospatial-specific failure modes, including handling large artifacts, selecting the wrong evidence source, losing spatial or temporal metadata, and applying invalid geometric operations. We introduce GeoFaham, a domain-specialized multi-agent system for geospatial disaster analytics. GeoFaham decomposes workflows into specialist agents for vector operations, map feature retrieval, imagery discovery, and raster analysis, coordinated by an Orchestrator with a dual-ledger control loop for dependency-aware planning, progress tracking, validation, and replanning. To support artifact-centric collaboration, GeoFaham uses a Response Store that persists full geospatial outputs and typed metadata outside the LLM context window while agents exchange compact identifiers and summaries. We also introduce GeoFaham-Bench, a 40-task benchmark grounded in 17 real-world disaster records, designed to evaluate multi-step geospatial reasoning, cross-source integration, raster-vector computation, artifact generation, and recovery under non-rigid ground truth. We evaluate GeoFaham on GeoFaham-Bench against strong general-purpose coding-agent baselines, including Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode. GeoFaham achieves the best overall performance, scoring 0.940 versus the next-best 0.879, while using 7.5 times fewer tokens. Our code and benchmark are publicly available at this https URL .

</details>


### [57] [Beyond Division of Labor: How Roles Shape Feedback and Recovery in Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03931)
*Chih-Hsuan Yang,Xinyang Li,Rajeev Thakur,Feng Yan*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: Roles in multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems allocate decisions as well as work. In a Planner--Executor--Reviewer team, the Reviewer's approval can determine when the team submits an answer and receives corrective feedback. We study both functions by varying role instructions while holding agents, topology, call budget, and ground-truth evaluator constant, using three open-weight models on Omni-MATH and two on SciBench. Removing roles largely eliminates functional specialization without lowering first-pass accuracy. After a failed first answer, however, submission decisions matter: a role-structured Reviewer often withholds approval, so its team submits less often and receives fewer evaluator verdicts. In an exploratory comparison with feedback available to both teams, the role-free team recovers more often across all five model--benchmark settings. Two further analyses support the importance of feedback opportunities. In a post hoc comparison at equal numbers of verdicts, the pooled recovery difference is small (role-structured minus role-free: $+0.009$, 95% interval $[-0.014,+0.033]$). In an exploratory intervention on $400$ Omni-MATH problems with gemma-4, keeping the role prompts but forcing submission in every cycle raises recovery from $0.198$ to $0.613$; the paired comparison detects no difference from the role-free team. The takeaway is to evaluate roles through recovery after failure as well as specialization. For systems with reliable external feedback, this requires measuring who may submit, how often the team receives feedback, and which agents can act on it.

### [58] [When Is Fresh AI Stock Analysis Worth It? Allocating a Limited Research Budget Across Price Updates, Deep Forecast Refreshes, and Editorial Reviews of Top Stock Picks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04348)
*Russlan Ramdowar*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: Must long-horizon AI investment research be rewritten every time stock prices move? Using 8,120 production reports on the same 203 stocks across four iPulse AI batches, we compare repricing existing targets, guarding them against price shocks, mechanically resetting old forecast growth, and generating fresh multi-agent reports. Ten matched configurations represent seven investment frameworks. Our primary economic evaluation selects Top 10 USD portfolios using one-year forecasts. Across two unchanged-model windows, guarded reuse averages 2.25%, versus 1.66% for SPY and 4.77% for fresh reports, after modeled trading costs and reference compute charges on a USD 100,000 account. Guarded reuse beats SPY in all three short windows, including the model-change transition. Extending the first holding window to nearly six months reverses the result: guarded reuse returns -11.26%, fresh reports +9.12%, and SPY +3.46%, motivating the thesis half-life question. Supporting quarter-forecast diagnostics show that mechanically re-anchoring old growth paths closes 98% of the MAE improvement over fixed targets, yet Fresh and Reset share only 1-4 of their Top 10 stocks. At Top 30, the unchanged-model portfolio comparison instead favors guarded reuse (4.17% versus 1.88%). Endpoint and concentration tests reveal the influence of horizon choices and exceptional winners. Nine production editions show substantial between-edition turnover, while every final editorial screen retains its own incoming list. Measured token workloads connect refresh costs to shared capital and realized break-even budgets. The resulting architecture separates continuous price monitoring from episodic thesis rebuilding and targeted editorial evidence checks.

### [59] [Distributed Marginal Return: A Communication-Efficient Algorithm for Multi-Agent Weapon Target Assignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04370)
*Kamal Mammadov,Glen Pearce,Helen Krause,Damith C. Ranasinghe*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: The Weapon-Target Assignment (WTA) problem in distributed multi-agent systems is challenged by limited situational awareness and communication constraints. Existing distributed methods, such as auction-consensus algorithms, typically assume task-value independence, a simplification that fails to capture the coupled effects of multi-weapon assignments. This paper introduces the Distributed Marginal Return (DMR) algorithm, a novel decentralized approach that generalizes auction-consensus frameworks. DMR enables agents to compute bids based on marginal return and uses a consensus protocol to resolve conflicts, allowing multiple non-conflicting proposals to be accepted in parallel for cooperative optimization with minimal communication. A key theoretical contribution is our proof that the marginal returns of non-conflicting bids are additive, a property that ensures global consistency and validates our parallel acceptance mechanism. Extensive simulations demonstrate that DMR significantly outperforms baseline algorithms in both solution quality and communication efficiency, offering a scalable and robust solution for real-world distributed command and control applications.

### [60] [AttriSwarm: Orchestrating Agent Swarms for Cross-Page Visual Attribution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04504)
*Suifeng Zhao,Zida Liu,Lei Sun,Xun Wang,Daojian Zeng,Jun Gao,Sujian Li*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) increasingly address knowledge-intensive tasks by integrating evidence scattered across multiple document pages into a final answer. Because such answers are synthesized from many pages, the link between the answer and its supporting visual evidence can become obscured, hindering verification and trust. Cross-page visual attribution is therefore essential: it requires identifying the supporting pages and localizing fine-grained evidence regions within them, thereby making multi-page reasoning transparent and auditable. Existing approaches either process multiple pages jointly or iteratively refine evidence within a single trajectory, risking cross-page context pollution and, for interactive methods, substantial sequential overhead. We introduce \textbf{AttriSwarm}, an agent-swarm framework that assigns these concerns to separate roles: a leader handles global cross-page reasoning, while subagents perform page-wise attribution in isolation and in parallel. To support training and evaluation, we construct \textbf{AttriDoc}, a cross-page QA dataset linking supporting pages to their annotated evidence regions, and use it for role-specific training of AttriSwarm, improving answer accuracy, page-level $F_1$, and region-level IoU over its training-free counterpart by an average of 18.94, 29.34, and 23.04 percentage points, respectively, across three open-source backbones and three datasets.

### [61] [Local Visibility Roadmaps in Continous Multi-agent Path Finding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04944)
*Kristýna Janovská,Pavel Surynek*

Main category: cs.MA

TL;DR: We address the problem of smooth continuous multi-agent path finding (SC-MAPF), where agents move in a continuous environment along smooth curves in continuous time. The paths for individual agents are searched in local visibility roadmaps that consider obstacles and other agents. A new algorithm is proposed in this work, which combines the previous algorithm CE-CBS for high-level search with any-angle path finding for local single-agent planning, where agents are to avoid obstacles, both static and other agents. The new algorithm is tested and compared to CE-CBS, the algorithm building individual paths using RRT$^*$, and SMT-CCBS algorithm, an algorithm for MAPF$_R$. Experimental results show various advantages of the new algorithm over CE-CBS and SMT-CCBS in comparable settings.

### [62] [GHOST Driver](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03649)
*Azhar Shaikh*

Main category: cs.OS

TL;DR: 本文提出 GHOST-Driver：一个基于 eBPF 的非侵入式 GPU 驱动侧可观测性框架，通过挂载 DRM 稳定 tracepoint 与部分 kprobe，分解 GPU 提交路径中的隐藏延迟（fence 等待、驱动提交开销、DMA 调度、中断合并），并按 SR-IOV/MIG 多租户上下文归因，指标导出至 Prometheus 与 OpenTelemetry，CPU 开销低于 2%。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: GPU 集群推理任务存在"利用率悖论"：nvidia-smi 报告的 GPU 利用率常超过 80%，但有效算力吞吐显著更低。原因是相当比例的"忙碌"时间实际消耗在用户态不可见的内核侧延迟上，包括 fence 等待、驱动提交开销、DMA 调度延迟与中断合并（interrupt coalescing）延迟。这些延迟深藏于 Linux 内核 GPU 驱动栈中，主要位于 DRM 子系统、GEM 缓冲区对象（BO）生命周期管理与 dma_fence 同步机制内。现有厂商工具（如 CUPTI）在 CUDA 用户态边界工作，无法观测内核驱动路径，导致运维与调度器无法区分"真实计算饱和"与"内核同步空转"，进而误判容量、错误配置资源配额与性能回归。

Method: 框架以非侵入式 eBPF 为基础，挂载于 DRM 子系统的稳定 tracepoint 以及精选 kprobe，实现亚微秒级时间分辨率的事件级追踪。覆盖六个关键提交阶段：(1) ioctl 入口；(2) GEM BO 校验/分配；(3) dma_fence 依赖解析；(4) 命令环（command ring）发射；(5) DMA 引擎调度；(6) 中断与 fence 信号。方法学关键点包括：利用内核已有 tracepoint 而非补丁侵入内核（避免影响生产稳定性与升级兼容性）；以 tracepoint 为主、kprobe 为辅的混合探针策略降低开销并规避函数内联/符号变动带来的失效风险；通过 per-tenant vGPU 上下文 ID 将各阶段事件与租户关联，实现 SR-IOV 与 MIG 环境下的多租户归因；最终将聚合后的 trace 指标以 Prometheus 与 OpenTelemetry 导出，融入既有可观测性栈。

Result: 摘要声称该框架能够提供 GPU 驱动提交路径的完整延迟分解视图，分辨率为亚微秒级，生产环境 CPU 开销低于 2%，可同时对六个提交阶段分别计时，并将延迟事件精确归属到具体租户的 vGPU 上下文，从而揭示出"报告利用率"与"有效吞吐"之间的差额来源。由于原文仅提供摘要，未给出具体的延迟降低幅度、归因分布数值或与基线工具的对比实验数据，量化结果有待全文验证。

Conclusion: GHOST-Driver 将 GPU 不可见的内核侧同步与提交开销转化为可观测、可归因、可导出的指标，使 nvidia-smi 等表层利用率指标得到解释性补充。其意义在于：把多租户 GPU 集群的容量规划、噪声邻居（noisy neighbor）诊断与推理服务 SLO 保障从猜测转向基于内核级延迟分解的实证依据；同时表明仅靠用户态 profiler 无法闭合 GPU 利用率与吞吐之间的差距。该工作定位为工程观测基础设施而非算子/内核优化，其对具体推理框架加速效果需与实际瓶颈（模型计算、内存带宽、通信）联合判断。

Abstract: AI inference workloads running on GPU clusters exhibit a well-documented utilization paradox: monitoring tools such as nvidia-smi regularly report GPU utilization figures above 80%, yet effective compute throughput is substantially lower. A significant fraction of reported utilization time is consumed by fence waits, driver submission overhead, DMA scheduling latency, and interrupt coalescing delays, none of which is visible to userspace profiling tools. These hidden latency components are embedded deep inside the Linux kernel GPU driver stack, primarily within the Direct Rendering Manager (DRM) subsystem, GEM buffer object lifecycle, and dma_fence synchronization infrastructure. Existing vendor profiling tools like CUPTI operate at the CUDA userspace boundary and provide no visibility into kernel-side driver paths. We present GHOST-Driver (GPU Host-Side Observability and Tracing for Drivers), a non-intrusive eBPF-based framework that attaches to stable DRM kernel tracepoints and select kprobes to expose the full latency decomposition of the GPU driver submission path with sub-microsecond resolution and CPU overhead below 2% in production. GHOST-Driver tracks six key submission stages (ioctl entry, GEM BO validation, dma_fence dependency resolution, command ring emission, DMA engine scheduling, and interrupt fence signaling) and correlates them with per-tenant vGPU context IDs for multi-tenant attribution in SR-IOV and MIG environments, exporting trace metrics to Prometheus and OpenTelemetry.

</details>
